title: Article 96 — The Speaker or the Deputy Speaker not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration

content.overview: Article 96 provides that the Speaker or Deputy Speaker shall not preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration. The Speaker has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the House while such a resolution is under consideration, but shall not be entitled to vote at all on such resolution or on any other matter during such proceedings (except a casting vote where provided in other contexts).
content.glance: Speaker/Deputy Speaker shall not preside during consideration of a resolution for his own removal.
content.study:
Article 96 is the Lok Sabha counterpart of Article 92. It prevents self-presiding on a removal resolution under Article 94.

Examination: no self-presiding; participation rights as in the article.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: While a resolution for removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker is under consideration, that person shall not preside.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can the Speaker preside over a resolution for his own removal?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Under Article 96, the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker shall not preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration.

keyTakeaways: Art 96: Speaker/Deputy Speaker not to preside on own removal resolution.
